# bulk_upload — High-Speed Batch File Upload/Download CLI for S3-Compatible Storage

> Rust CLI tool. Extracts URLs from JSON, downloads in parallel, uploads to S3-compatible storage.
> Single binary, zero dependencies, cross-platform.

## Command Syntax

```
bulk_upload jq [JSON_TEXT | @FILE | -] [--s3 <CONFIG_PATH>] [--prefix <S3_PREFIX>] [--concurrency <N>] [--json]
```

### Arguments
- `JSON_TEXT`: JSON string, `@path/to/file.json`, or `-`/omitted for stdin (stdin must be piped). All HTTP/HTTPS URLs are extracted recursively.
- `--s3 <path>`: S3 credential file (dotenv format). Optional: when omitted, the same S3_* keys are read from environment variables
- `--prefix <prefix>`: S3 key prefix for uploaded files (default: empty)
- `--concurrency <N>`: Files per concurrent batch, 1-100 (default: 10)
- `--json`: One JSON envelope on stdout; data = {bucket, total_urls, total_success, total_failed, batches, files:[{source_url, s3_key, status, error}]}

### Examples

```bash
# Upload from inline JSON
bulk_upload jq '{"urls":["https://example.com/a.png","https://example.com/b.png"]}' --s3 .s3 --prefix assets/

# Upload from stdin
cat urls.json | bulk_upload jq - --s3 .s3 --prefix textures/v2/ --concurrency 10

# With JSON output
bulk_upload --json jq '{"img":"https://example.com/photo.jpg"}' --s3 .s3
```

## Config Format

S3 credential file (`.s3`) uses dotenv format:

```env
S3_BUCKET=my-bucket
S3_ACCESS_KEY=your-access-key
S3_SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key
S3_ENDPOINT=https://your-account.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
S3_REGION=auto
```

## Supported Storage Providers

- AWS S3: `https://s3.amazonaws.com`
- Cloudflare R2: `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`
- Aliyun OSS: `https://<bucket>.<region>.aliyuncs.com`
- iDrive E2: `https://<endpoint>.idrivee2.com`
- MinIO: `http://<host>:9000`
- Any S3-compatible endpoint with path-style addressing

## Behavior

1. Parses JSON input recursively to find all `http://` and `https://` strings
2. Deduplicates URLs while preserving order
3. Splits URLs into batches based on `--concurrency`
4. Downloads each batch concurrently using async HTTP client
5. Uploads successful downloads to S3 with `--prefix` prepended to filename
6. Filename extracted from URL path (query params stripped)
7. Reports success/failure count

## Exit Codes

- `0`: All files processed successfully (also when no URL was found; see `warnings`)
- `2`: Usage error (bad flags, no input and stdin is a terminal)
- `3`: Input error (invalid JSON, missing/incomplete S3 config)
- `4`: External failure (every URL failed to download or upload)
- `5`: Partial (some URLs failed; per-URL results in data.files)

## Installation

```bash
# One-line install (Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS Intel/ARM64, Windows-Git-Bash)
curl -fsSL https://r2.gamesci-lite.com/r_lit/bulk_upload/install.sh | bash

# Custom install dir
curl -fsSL https://r2.gamesci-lite.com/r_lit/bulk_upload/install.sh | INSTALL_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin bash

# Build from source
cargo build --release
# Binary at: target/release/bulk_upload
```

## System Requirements

- OS: Linux (x86_64), macOS (ARM64)
- Binary size: 3-4MB (statically linked, stripped)
- Memory: Proportional to concurrency level, typically <50MB
- No runtime dependencies

## Use Cases for AI Agents

- Batch upload generated assets to cloud storage after processing
- Migrate files between S3-compatible providers
- Download and re-upload content from API responses
- CI/CD artifact publishing

## Performance Characteristics

- Async I/O (Tokio runtime), saturates available bandwidth
- Zero-copy streaming, minimal memory allocation
- Handles thousands of files without memory growth
- Configurable concurrency for resource-constrained environments

## Machine Call Contract (r_lit CLI contract v1)

- spec: docs/cli-contract.md (repo root); implementation: crates/rlit_cli
- json: `--json` is global; stdout carries exactly one JSON envelope, also on failure; logs go to stderr
- envelope: {"contract":1, "ok", "tool":"bulk_upload", "version", "command", "data", "artifacts":[{"path","role","bytes","sha256"}], "error":null|{"code","kind","message"}, "warnings"?}
- exit_codes: 0 ok, 1 runtime, 2 usage, 3 input, 4 external, 5 partial (ok=false, data still complete)
- schema: `bulk_upload __schema` prints JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) per subcommand, with x-cli (argv mapping, io role), x-effects, x-env, x-stdin, x-note
- non_interactive: never prompts
- effects: jq=external; x-env: S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY, S3_SECRET_KEY, S3_ENDPOINT, S3_REGION; x-stdin: JSON document
